objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, let's continue.', approving FLAT-STATES-20261107-001's recommendation): prove resolution width Theta(sqrt n) for the knot's sphere and a width bound for grid Sperner, or locate the obstruction. Route: Duplicator keeps a label state whose vortex avoids every closed walk through pebbles that could pin it; the window criterion shows such walks are short relative to their pebbles, so a covering argument bounds the trapped area by O(pebbles^2). Test whether the same argument works on the Sperner disk, whose fixed boundary is free for Spoiler.
status: Complete 2026-11-07: the sphere's count needs resolution width Theta(sqrt n) (every refutation of the octahedral knot sphere K_k has width >= c*k - 1; O(k) suffices), and grid Sperner needs width Theta(m) (so does Itsykson et al.'s Sperner CSP). Duplicator keeps the vortex where pebbles are sparse: by the exact window criterion every obstruction is a closed walk with a bounded number of steps per pebble, so pebbles trap only O(pebbles^2) area; on the disk, walks through the free boundary stay near it. The winding-control lemma named by FLAT-STATES was not needed. Size stays open. Next: resolution size via Dantchev-Riis tiling games with random label states per zone (2/3).
stop_rule: Stop when width Omega(sqrt n) for the knot sphere is proved or refuted by a trapping configuration, and the grid-Sperner width is proved, reduced to a named lemma, or shown to need a different argument.
title: Resolution width of the sphere's count and of grid Sperner
